item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q001_histone_related_proteins","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08, the canonical core histones are not merely all-alpha lookalikes: they sit in class a, All alpha proteins, inside fold a.22, Histone-fold, and the only curated superfamily under that fold is a.22.1, Histone-fold. The manually named sibling families in that superfamily are the related groups: a.22.1.1 Nucleosome core histones, containing H2A, H2B, H3, H4 and macro-H2A.1; a.22.1.2 Archaeal histone; a.22.1.3 TBP-associated factors, TAFs, which also contains histone-fold domains from CHRAC-14/16, NC2 alpha/beta, NF-Y beta/gamma, Son of sevenless, and several TAF(II) proteins; and a.22.1.4 Bacterial histone-fold protein, represented by Aq_328- and TTHA1479-like proteins. These Archaeal, TAF/NC2/NF-Y/CHRAC/SoS, and bacterial proteins are therefore histone-related at the SCOPe superfamily level: stronger than a shared all-alpha class or fold shape and interpreted as remote homology to the core-histone fold, but separated into different families rather than treated as eukaryotic nucleosome core histones or one-to-one H2A/H2B/H3/H4 orthologs. SCOPe also has an a.22.1.0 automated-matches family under the same superfamily; those entries can support placement in the histone-fold superfamily but should not be read as another curated named family. Functional transfer across these families is unsafe without additional evidence: for example, TAFs, NC2, NF-Y, and CHRAC are transcription or chromatin-regulatory histone-fold domains, not nucleosome core histones; bacterial hypothetical proteins and archaeal histones are distinct families. Likewise, a SCOPe domain or automated match is a curated/reference structural classification, not a complete domain inventory for an external sequence, and no AlphaFold or 90%-identity representative chain hit was used here to infer boundaries or function. A protein named histone is not automatically in this a.22 histone-fold group either: SCOPe classifies linker histone H1/H5 globular domains separately in the a.4 DNA/RNA-binding 3-helical-bundle fold and the a.4.5 winged-helix superfamily.","evidence_used":["get_scop_node: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/a.22; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/a.22/parents","list_scop_children: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/a.22/children?limit=100","list_scop_children: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/a.22.1/children?limit=100","list_scop_children: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/47114/children?limit=100","list_scop_children: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/47129/children?limit=100","list_scop_children: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/47134/children?limit=100","list_scop_children: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/101318/children?limit=100","list_scop_children: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/238448/children?limit=100","resolve_scop_identifier: /api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/1hst","get_scop_pdb_entry: /api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1hst; /api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1hst/domains","get_scop_node: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/a.4.5.13; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/a.4.5.13/parents"]}]}
